descriptionChirho: To sacrifice or offer a cultic sacrifice to God or to idols, encompassing all Qal forms where the multilingual glosses consistently indicate a ritual religious offering (Hindi बलि/बलिदान, Arabic ذَبَحَ in sacrificial context, Swahili kutoa dhabihu, Korean 제사하다); this is the primary and most frequent sense of זָבַח.

The Piel intensive stem of זָבַח, denoting habitual, repeated, or emphatic sacrificial activity; while the glosses overlap with the Qal cultic sense (English 'sacrificing/sacrificed', Hindi बलिदान, Swahili dhabihu), the Piel stem marks iterative or intensive aspect, often describing ongoing idolatrous or persistent sacrificial practices.

To slaughter or butcher an animal, with the focus on the physical act of killing rather than the cultic offering; distinguished from the sacrifice sense by multilingual glosses using slaughter vocabulary (English 'slaughtered', Spanish matarás/degolláis/degolló, Korean 잡았다, Swahili kuchinja/akachinja rather than kutoa dhabihu).
